newsitem.title: UK: Pakistan Telecom convertible bond price soars.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan Telecom convertible bond price soars.

text.p: A $150 million five-year bond exchangeable into Pakistan Telecommunications Co Ltd (PTCL) shares was well-received by investors and its price rose sharply, dealers said on Thursday.
Launched at a price of 100, the deal was quoted at around 102 at 1430 GMT.
"The deal has gone extremely well and is trading towards 102," a banker at joint lead manager Nomura said.
"The distribution was evenly split between Asia, Europe and Britain. There was no selling into the U.S."
The bond was issued by the Pakistani government but is exchangeable into PTCL shares as part of its privatisation.
The head of the Karachi Stock Exchange said earlier the exchangeable bond had attracted $650 million of orders.
"The bond got a very good response abroad," Arif Habib told Reuters in Karachi, adding this would boost confidence among foreign investors.
The Nomura official said the figure was roughly right but he was unable to give an exact amount.
"This transaction is good for the government of Pakistan, which has not done a lot of issues in the international market," the Nomura official said.
"The good reception will benefit their upcoming deal, although their Eurobond will go to a different set of investors."
Last week Pakistan mandated ANZ Investment Bank to underwrite a three-year Eurobond. Investor presentations will be held in the middle of March, with launch by the end of March.
Pakistan is rated B2 by Moody's Investors Service and B plus by Standard & Poor's.
